channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Ten x Ten – 18th Annual Small Works · Midwest Center for Photography
item.description: Annual small works exhibition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (November 14 – December 31, 2026). Celebrates creative expression within the square photographic format. All works are 10"×10" and priced at $200 each. MWCP provides printing at no cost to selected artists. Open to all photographers internationally. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: $30 framing fee. Prize: None listed.

item.title: HOME · Decode Gallery
item.description: Exploring the multifaceted nature of home — as feeling, memory, sanctuary, physical space, heritage, or identity. Photographers invited to capture domestic spaces, loved ones, landscapes, or personal belonging. At least 26 images selected for exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Epson printers with Ilford Pearl paper, museum-quality 22×22 white framing and custom matting. Open worldwide to all skill levels. Exhibition June 6 – 27, 2026. — Deadline: April 18, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: FOTOHOF>CALLING
item.description: Biennial open call for contemporary photographic projects. Around 25 artists are selected for online publication on the FOTOHOF>CALLING platform and in the FOTOHOF>CALLING Magazine. 10 finalists are invited to present their projects in Salzburg on October 3, 2026, with an open-air projection on Inge-Morath-Platz. Projects must be no older than three years and never exhibited in institutional settings (museums, galleries, festivals). Student/university work and residency programs are exempt from this rule. Open to artists who reside, work, or stay in Europe. — Deadline: April 26, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication + exhibition.

item.title: Martin House Creative Residency 2026
item.description: 2–4 week project-based residency at Frank Lloyd Wright's Darwin D. Martin House in Buffalo, New York. Residents live in the Gardener's Cottage on campus and create new work inspired by the architecture, design, landscape, and social history of Martin House. Open to artists working in any discipline including photography, writing, and research. Residents receive $5,000 stipend paid in two installments and up to $1,000 travel allowance for non-local applicants. Residency term runs June–October 2026. Must deliver a free public program, performance, or exhibition sharing work with the community. Requires US social security number. Application window March 30 – April 24, 2026. — Deadline: April 24, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000 stipend.

item.title: Dodho Magazine #37
item.description: International open call for print edition #37 of Dodho Magazine. Conceived as an artistic and curatorial volume rather than a traditional magazine. Each selected photographer receives 20 full pages with visual rhythm, curatorial text, and breathing room for images. Two submission modes: Magazine Mode for a full portfolio feature, or Cover Mode for the front page. International distribution across galleries, festivals, museums, and institutions. 36 prior editions featuring 216 photographers from 32 countries. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: €45. Prize: Publication + international distribution.

item.title: Odesa Workshop — Environmental Consequences of War in Ukraine · Inland
item.description: 7-month hybrid workshop for Ukrainian or Ukraine-based documentary photographers documenting the environmental consequences of war. 10–12 participants selected. Program includes online lectures (June 2026), live sessions with international editors and experts, a 3-day in-person lab in Odesa (September 11–13, 2026), and individual mentorship through November 2026. One participant receives a €1,500 production grant. Supported by JournalismFund Europe. — Deadline: May 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €1,500 production grant.

item.title: Loghaven Artist Residency 2027
item.description: Residency on 90 acres of forested land in Knoxville, Tennessee for practicing artists at any career stage. Sessions range from 2–6 weeks between February and October 2027. All fellows receive an $850/week living stipend, travel subsidy ($400–$800 on a sliding scale), and up to $200 in materials shipping reimbursement. Disciplines include visual arts, writing, dance, music composition, theater, and interdisciplinary work. Applicants must be 21+, live 120+ miles from Knoxville, and have legal US work authorization. International artists are not eligible. Applications open June 1, 2026. Submit 8 JPEG images for visual art via SlideRoom. — Deadline: July 15, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $850/week stipend.

item.title: FMoPA 2026 International Photography Competition
item.description: International photography competition open to photographers worldwide. Submit up to 15 images across 7 categories: People/Portraits, Places/Landscape, Nature/Science/Animals, Documentation/Photojournalism, Still Life, Abstract, and Conceptual. Best in Competition receives $1,000 cash prize. Category winners receive goods and services. Winning works exhibited June 16 – August 2, 2026 at FMoPA in Tampa's Ybor City District. — Deadline: April 22, 2026. Fee: $10. Prize: $1,000 + exhibition.

item.title: Fotograf Magazine 2026 Open Call
item.description: Open call for publication in Fotograf Magazine, a leading international photography publication based in Prague. Two selected projects published in the next printed issue. Open to professionals, amateurs, and students submitting independent fine-art photography or moving-image projects. Submit CV, portfolio PDF, and project description with images via email. — Deadline: April 30, 2026. Fee: €35/project. Prize: Publication in Fotograf Magazine.

item.title: Grenze Arsenali Fotografici 2026 Open Call
item.description: Open call for the ninth edition of Grenze - Arsenali Fotografici international photography festival in Verona. Theme: Nachleben. Three artists selected for exhibition during the festival opening September 2026. — Deadline: April 30, 2026. Fee: €28. Prize: Exhibition at Grenze festival.

item.title: Photography 4 Humanity / Fotografiska Global Prize 2026
item.description: Global photography prize exploring the theme HOME — safety, belonging, identity, memory, loss, and place. Open to photographers worldwide. Selected photographs exhibited at United Nations Headquarters in New York on Human Rights Day (December 10, 2026), guest-curated by James Nachtwey. — Deadline: July 12, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition at UN Headquarters.

item.title: Minimalist Photography Awards 2026
item.description: Seventh edition of the international award celebrating minimalist photography as a visual language. Open to photographers worldwide. Submit single images or series (2–7 images) across 12 categories including Abstract, Architecture, Fine Art, Landscape, Long Exposure, Portrait, and Street. Grand prize: €2,000 cash, hand-crafted trophy, title of Minimalist Photographer of the Year, and inclusion in the official annual book. Earlybird deadline May 1; final deadline June 2, 2026. — Deadline: June 2, 2026. Fee: €20–€35. Prize: €2,000 + book + exhibition.

item.title: Villa Lena Foundation — Artist Residency 2027
item.description: Residency program for artists of all disciplines in a 19th-century villa in Tuscany, Italy. Residencies run 4–5 weeks between April and October 2027. Includes studio space, accommodation, and half-board meals five days a week. Residency fee of €150/week covers room, studio, and meals. Artists must donate a completed work to the foundation's collection. Access to ceramic and wood workshops, screening room, and weekly excursions. — Deadline: April 30, 2026. Fee: €21. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Human Depiction · Midwest Center for Photography
item.description: International portrait photography exhibition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (May 1–25, 2026). Seeks photographs capturing the essence of human subjects — emotional gestures, visual expressions, and the full range of personality. Individual images evaluated on merit. Selected artists' work printed and framed by MWCP for gallery display. — Deadline: April 10, 2026. Fee: $50/5 images. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Blossom · Midwest Center for Photography
item.description: International floral photography exhibition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (June 5–22, 2026). Celebrates photographs of flowers and plants in all forms — from nature photography to still-life approaches. Open to all photographic media and styles. Selected artists' work printed and framed by MWCP for gallery display. — Deadline: May 1, 2026. Fee: $50/5 images. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Traversing Terrain · Midwest Center for Photography
item.description: International landscape and cityscape photography exhibition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (July 11–27, 2026). Features photographs describing and documenting natural and man-made landscapes — urban, suburban, and rural environments. All photographic media welcome. Selected artists' work printed and framed by MWCP for gallery display. — Deadline: May 1, 2026. Fee: $50/5 images. Prize: None listed.

item.title: White: Absence of Color · Midwest Center for Photography
item.description: International achromatic photography exhibition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (August 7–24, 2026). Explores photography emphasizing the lightest end of the color spectrum — minimal color saturation conveying striking imagery and psychological impact. All photographic media welcome. Selected artists' work printed and framed by MWCP for gallery display. — Deadline: May 1, 2026. Fee: $50/5 images. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Developed Work 2026 · Midwest Center for Photography
item.description: National photography fellowship competition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (October 2–26, 2026). Open to all US-based photographers. Seeks thematically developed bodies of work with cohesive conceptual frameworks demonstrating the pulse of contemporary American photography. Winner receives the $200 Developed Work Fellowship Award and one year of online representation by MWCP. — Deadline: July 1, 2026. Fee: $50/5 images. Prize: $200 fellowship + exhibition.

item.title: AAP Magazine #57 Portrait · All About Photo
item.description: Portrait photography competition exploring humanity through portraiture. Winners receive $1,000 cash, publication in AAP Magazine #57, and global recognition. All styles welcome including studio, candid, self-portraits, and conceptual work. Open to professional and amateur photographers aged 18+. Submit a cohesive body of work or portfolio. Judged on creativity, originality, and visual impact. — Deadline: April 28, 2026. Fee: $30–$35. Prize: $1,000.

item.title: nice;04 · midwest nice art
item.description: Fourth annual Midwest Nice Art national juried exhibition. Open theme — a survey of contemporary artists exploring personal and social narratives. Juried by co-founders Tim Rickett and Epiphany Knedler. First prize $300, second $200, third $100, four honorable mentions at $50 each. Physical exhibition at JFAC Gallery, Northern State University, Aberdeen, South Dakota (July 13–September 11, 2026). Work must be framed and ready for exhibition. — Deadline: May 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $300.

item.title: Photo of the Season — Worth a Thousand Words · The Image Flow
item.description: Seasonal photography competition inviting powerful standalone images that tell a compelling story. Theme: Worth a Thousand Words — narrative, emotion, and storytelling. Open worldwide. First prize $150, second $100, third $50 plus two honorable mentions. All winners featured in gallery, newsletter, website, and social media. Accepts film, digital, alternative process, and printmaking. — Deadline: June 20, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: $150.

item.title: Mangrove Photography Awards 2026 · Mangrove Action Project
item.description: Annual international conservation photography competition celebrating the beauty and importance of mangrove ecosystems. Six categories: Wildlife, People, Landscape, Threats, Underwater, and Conservation Stories (portfolio of 6 images). Overall Mangrove Photographer of the Year receives $1,000; category winners $250–$750. Young Mangrove Photographer of the Year for entrants aged 23 and under. People's Choice Award announced in August. Free entry, open to all photographers worldwide, any age and skill level. Judged by Esther Horvath, Karine Aigner, and Dhritiman Mukherjee. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,000 + category prizes.

item.title: Better Photography Magazine Photographer of the Year 2026
item.description: 19th edition of Australia's premier photography competition. Four categories: Emotive Portraiture, Classic Landscapes, Revealing Nature, and Open. Every entry professionally scored by three AIPP Grand Masters of Photography with written feedback. Bronze, Silver, and Gold designations awarded based on quality. Category winners receive AUD $750 each; overall Photographer of the Year receives AUD $2,000. Entrants with four or more images eligible for the overall award. International entries welcome. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: AUD $20/image. Prize: AUD $2,000 + category prizes.

item.title: Fieldwork Photo Journal — Issue Two: The Embodied Weight of Place
item.description: Print publication exploring how place is not experienced neutrally — landscapes, interiors, and built environments carry histories that shape how they are felt. Featured photographer: Kristine Potter. Up to 30 photographers selected. First 6 images included in fee, additional images $5 each (max 12). JPG only, longest edge 1500px at 150 dpi. Publication date: Fall/Winter 2026. — Deadline: May 6, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Pearl Press — Issue No. 28: Utopia
item.description: Online publication open call themed 'Utopia' — escapism, joy, acceptance, community. Submit via email with name, short bio, title and description of work. Visual work must be at least 300 dpi. No min or max on number of submissions. Selected work published in Issue No. 28 and featured on Instagram. — Deadline: April 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Delfina Foundation — India Residency 2026
item.description: Twelve-week fully funded residency at the Delfina Foundation in London for contemporary visual artists based in India. Supported by The Charles Wallace India Trust and The Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation. Residency runs January 5 to March 28, 2027 (winter season). Apply via Cognito Forms — read the Guidance Notes document before applying. — Deadline: April 13, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency.

item.title: The Flow 2026 Photo Contest · Flow Trip Magazine
item.description: Annual photo contest presented by Kodak with $50,000 in total prizes across five categories: Film, Surf, Nature, Energy, and Oneness. Grand prize of $4,000 per category, plus finalist and honorable mention awards. Open to professional and amateur photographers worldwide. All entries considered for publication in The Photo Issue of Flow Trip Magazine. Winners announced June 2026. AI-generated or AI-altered images not accepted. — Deadline: April 24, 2026. Fee: $6/image. Prize: $4,000 per category + publication.

item.title: Artadia Awards 2026 — San Francisco Bay Area
item.description: Unrestricted merit-based grants for contemporary visual artists including photographers. Three awardees receive $15,000 each. Two-round jury process: curators review applications, then conduct 45-minute virtual studio visits with finalists. Applicants must have resided in one of nine Bay Area counties for at least two years. Cannot be enrolled in an art degree program or have previously received Artadia awards of $10,000 or more. Application period: May 1 – June 1, 2026. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $15,000.

item.title: Joy and the Everyday 2026 · Atlanta Photography Group
item.description: Themed exhibition exploring how photographers capture joy in everyday moments. Juried by Emilia Mickevicius, Ph.D., Norton Family Assistant Curator of Photography at the Center for Creative Photography. 24 images selected for print exhibition in the Maloof Gallery at APG, Atlanta, June 16 – July 17, 2026. Open to APG members. Scholarships available. — Deadline: May 1, 2026. Fee: $35–$95. Prize: None listed.

item.title: #filmisnotdead 2026 · Atlanta Photography Group
item.description: Juried exhibition celebrating analog photography. Open to all traditional processes including film, wet plate, cyanotype, and other analog techniques. No theme — open subject matter. Juried by Michael Behlen, Founder and Publisher of Analog Forever Magazine. 30 images selected for the Main Gallery at APG, Atlanta, June 16 – July 17, 2026. Open to APG members. Scholarships available. — Deadline: May 1, 2026. Fee: $35–$95. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Apparently in America — Artist Award 2026
item.description: Photography award exploring the myth and meaning of American identity today. Submit 10–20 images reflecting on cultural, political, and personal dimensions of U.S. identity. $500 prize for selected artist plus up to three honorable mentions. Fee waivers available for those experiencing financial hardship. Founded by curator Francesca Hummler. — Deadline: July 4, 2026. Fee: $10. Prize: $500.

item.title: Project Space Residency 2027 · Visual Studies Workshop
item.description: Four-week residency for photographers, filmmakers, and media artists in Rochester, NY. Up to 12 residents selected annually. $1,000 stipend, $250 supply budget, $500 travel budget for non-local residents. Private studio with 24/7 access, analog darkroom, digital printing, and accessible housing. Curator consultations and public engagement opportunities. Over 50 years of supporting experimental work. Fee waivers available. — Deadline: May 18, 2026. Fee: $10. Prize: $1,000 stipend + residency.

item.title: Taylor Wessing Photo Portrait Prize 2026 · National Portrait Gallery
item.description: One of the world's most prestigious portrait photography competitions. Open to photographers worldwide, aged 18+. Submit up to 6 portraits taken after 1 January 2025. First prize £15,000, second £3,000, third £2,000. Selected works exhibited at the National Portrait Gallery in London from November 2026 to January 2027. The prize celebrates contemporary portraiture, interpreting 'portrait' in its widest sense — photography concerned with portraying people with an emphasis on their identity as individuals. — Deadline: April 21, 2026. Fee: £22/image. Prize: £15,000.

item.title: Barbara Spohr Memorial Award for Photography 2027 · Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity
item.description: Annual award supporting Canadian contemporary photography. One mid-career photographer receives a fully funded month-long self-directed residency at Banff Centre (January 18 – February 12, 2027). Access to the Crich Studio with private black and white analogue darkroom, facilitated digital print production, and technical photography support. Full scholarship covering tuition, single accommodation, and meal plan ($7,600 CAD value). $1,000 CAD materials allowance plus travel bursary. Applicants must have a minimum of ten exhibitions in a professional context and 8–15 years of professional arts experience. — Deadline: June 17, 2026. Fee: $35 CAD. Prize: $1,000 CAD + residency.

item.title: Global Peace Photo Award 2026 · Global Peace Photo Award
item.description: Annual international award recognizing photographs that express the idea of peaceful coexistence. Open to all photographers worldwide. Winners receive the Alfred Fried Peace Medal, cash prizes, and travel and accommodation to the award ceremony at the Austrian Parliament in Vienna (September 24, 2026). Submissions may be single photographs or photo projects with up to 12 images per project. All submissions may be included in international exhibitions. Separate Children's Peace Image category for photographers under 15. — Deadline: May 24, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €11,000.

item.title: Working Assumptions Project Grants 2026 · Working Assumptions
item.description: Six $10,000 unrestricted grants awarded annually to support photography-based projects that inspire audiences to look at family in new, meaningful ways. Proposals may employ photography or photo-based art for journalistic, artistic, therapeutic, educational, or research purposes. Projects must have been initiated prior to the application deadline. Grant period runs October 2026 to June 2027. Application window opens May 1, 2026. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000 × 6 grants.

item.title: EMERGE 2026 · Midwest Center for Photography
item.description: Annual fellowship for emerging photographers. Open to all emerging photographers worldwide working in any photographic medium. Twenty photographers selected for group exhibition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (September 4–21, 2026). One photographer receives the $200 EMERGE Fellowship Award plus one year of online representation by MWCP. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: $50/5 images. Prize: $200 fellowship + exhibition.

item.title: The Photo Review 41st Annual International Photography Competition
item.description: 41st edition of one of photography's most respected annual competitions. Juried by Dr. Sarah Kennel, Aaron Siskind Curator of Photography at the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts. Selected work exhibited at the Woodmere Art Museum in Philadelphia and published in The Photo Review journal. $1,000 purchase prize from Haverford College plus equipment and printing prizes. All entrants receive a full-color catalogue. — Deadline: May 20, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: $1,000 purchase prize + exhibition + publication.

item.title: Lisbon Street Photo Fest: Open Call 2026
item.description: 2nd edition. Street photography open call in two categories: Singles (individual photos) and Series (10–15 images). Finalists exhibited at Faculdade de Belas-Artes da Universidade de Lisboa during festival weekend, 25–27 September 2026. €4,000 in cash prizes plus VSCO Pro memberships. Photos must be captured after 1 January 2024. No AI-generated content or watermarks. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: €10/image, €40/series. Prize: €4,000 + exhibition.

item.title: PowerLines Documentary Photography Fellowship
item.description: Three-month documentary photography fellowship from PowerLines, a national nonprofit focused on modernizing public utilities. The fellow documents the human experience of rising utility costs across the United States. $30,000 stipend distributed over three months (May 15 – August 15, 2026). Joint ownership of all images produced. Fellows may accept non-conflicting external assignments during the fellowship. Applicants must have at least three years of professional documentary or photojournalism experience. — Deadline: April 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $30,000 stipend.

item.title: Tulsa Artist Fellowship 2027–2029
item.description: Three-year fellowship for visual artists in Tulsa, Oklahoma. Ten fellows selected from an open call. Each receives a $150,000 project development stipend, $36,000 housing stipend, fully subsidized private studio (337–583 sq ft), $3,600 studio assistant stipend, and $3,600 health/wellness stipend. Access to shared ceramics studio, woodshop, metal equipment, media lab, archival printer, performance space, and podcast studio. Fellows must relocate to Tulsa for the full three-year term (January 2027–December 2029). Applicants must be 25+ with at least five years of experience in the arts and a project proposal with community engagement focus. U.S. citizens, permanent residents, O-1 visa holders, or Tribal ID holders eligible. Applications open April 7, 2026. — Deadline: May 7, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $150,000 stipend + housing + studio.

item.title: Women's Studio Workshop — Studio Workspace Residency
item.description: 4–6 week residency for artists at any career stage at Women's Studio Workshop in Rosendale, NY. Choose from five studios: intaglio, letterpress, papermaking, screenprinting, or darkroom photography. Housing and studio space fully subsidized. Staff assistance available. Artists work independently and provide their own materials. Residencies take place September through June, 1–2 years after application. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Housing + studio.

item.title: Abstract 2026 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: International photography exhibition on the theme of abstract. Submit images exploring abstract concepts in any photographic style. Selected work displayed in a month-long gallery exhibition in Glasgow, with work also appearing in an online gallery on the gallery's website. Images printed on Fujifilm photographic paper and framed in gallery frames. Photographers retain all copyright. — Deadline: April 24, 2026. Fee: Free (£48 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Portrait 2026 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: International photography exhibition on the theme of portrait. Open to everyone. Selected work displayed in a month-long gallery exhibition in Glasgow, with work also appearing in an online gallery on the gallery's website. Images printed on Fujifilm photographic paper and framed in gallery frames. Photographers retain all copyright. — Deadline: April 24, 2026. Fee: Free (£48 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Rancho Linda Vista — Summer Artist Residency 2026
item.description: One-month summer residency for visual artists at Rancho Linda Vista, a historic arts community on 100+ acres in Oracle, Arizona. Resident receives a furnished one-bedroom house, separate studio space, and $1,000 stipend. Access to swimming pool, library, and wilderness trails. Open studio exhibit at conclusion of stay. Available for July or August 2026. Must provide own transportation and materials. MFA preferred but not required. — Deadline: April 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,000 stipend.

item.title: La Embajada 2026 · El Local
item.description: Third edition of La Embajada, a programme promoting contemporary Spanish photography within the European circuit through an exhibition during the opening week of Rencontres d'Arles. Six projects selected, each artist receiving €1,400 fee. Selected photographers exhibit during the festival's opening week (July 6–13, 2026) and participate in active mediation with audiences. La Embajada creates a temporary 'embassy' to showcase photographic projects and foster professional connections at the epicentre of world photography. Organised by El Local (independent space for contemporary photography in Madrid) in partnership with Plataforma Fotografía e Imagen, with support from Spain's Ministry of Culture. Submit one project per applicant via digital form. Work must be produced and exhibition-ready. Physical presence in Arles during opening week is mandatory. — Deadline: April 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €1,400 artist fee + exhibition.

item.title: 12th Annual International Open Call · Rhode Island Center for Photographic Arts
item.description: International showcase for contemporary voices in photography with no theme or prompt, bringing together image makers from around the world to survey current photographic practice. Open to all photographers 18+ worldwide working in any photographic process or technique. Juried by Crista Dix, Executive Director of the Griffin Museum of Photography. Up to 15 photographs accepted per entry. Exhibition at RICPA gallery in Providence, Rhode Island from July 16 through August 15, 2026. Opening reception July 16. Members receive 20% discount on entry fees. Work must be exhibition-ready, maximum 48 inches including frame. Delivery of accepted work by July 11. — Deadline: May 3, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: $250 / $150 / $75.

item.title: APhF Pick:26 Book Award
item.description: Annual juried photobook award from the Hellenic Centre of Photography as part of Athens Photo Festival. Open to all photobooks worldwide produced or published between January 2025 and March 2026 with a minimum edition of 100 copies. Winner receives €2,000 cash prize and inclusion in the main festival exhibition programme at Benaki Museum. Ten photobooks featured in the APhF:26 print catalogue, twenty shortlisted and exhibited at Benaki Museum / Pireos 138. All submitted works added to the APhF Library and Athens Photo Research Center. Submit online entry form, cover image, project description, artist biography, and mail two physical copies to the Hellenic Center of Photography in Athens. €15 for each additional project by the same applicant. — Deadline: April 28, 2026. Fee: €25. Prize: €2,000 + exhibition.

item.title: British Wildlife Photography Awards 2026
item.description: Annual photography competition celebrating the diversity and beauty of British wildlife, now in its fourteenth year. Open to photographers worldwide, but all images must be taken in Britain or the British Isles. Twelve categories including Animal Behaviour, Animal Portraits, Botanical Britain, Black and White, British Seasons, Coast and Marine, Habitat, Hidden Britain, Urban Wildlife, Wild Woods, Documentary Series, and Video. Photos must be taken after January 1, 2019. Youth competition (17 and under) is free to enter. Winners announced March 2027 and featured in the Collection 14 coffee table book and a UK touring exhibition. Post-processing permitted but no compositing, sky swapping, or object removal. Proceeds from auction of award-winning prints donated to Birds on the Brink charity. AI-generated images strictly prohibited. — Deadline: June 7, 2026. Fee: £35–£40. Prize: £10,000 total + book + touring exhibition.

item.title: JGS Fellowship for Photography 2026 · New York Foundation for the Arts
item.description: Annual fellowship awarding $8,000 each to five photographers working in New York State outside New York City. Supports traditional and experimental photography including light-based work, alternative processes, or any form in which photography or photographic techniques are pivotal. Applicants must be 25 or older, current full-time residents of eligible NY State regions for at least 12 months, and not enrolled in a degree-seeking programme. Past recipients are not eligible. Applications submitted via Submittable. Notification of results in summer 2026. — Deadline: May 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $8,000.
